# Absurd AI characters and mascots in the Italian-brainrot format

**A food or object, an animal and one human detail become an original mascot with a turnaround sheet ready for video.**

<p><img src="https://s3.varg.ai/files/194b94d0-58ff-4e8b-91de-4f1959d04013/file_7701d7fee03c.webp" alt="Turnaround sheets of absurd 3D mascots crossfade: a bread T-rex in a beret, a grumpy cactus mail carrier and a nervous sheep accountant." width="480"></p>

Makes absurd AI characters and mascots people share, on varg: hybrids of a food or object, an animal and one human detail (a T-rex made of bread in a beret, a grumpy cactus mail carrier, a nervous sheep accountant), in a 3D family-film, clay stop-motion or photoreal look, as a turnaround sheet ready for scenes and video. The Italian-brainrot format with original characters. Use when someone asks for an absurd, funny, weird or brainrot character, a creature, a talking animal or object, a food character, or a brand mascot. Part of varg-character-design (definition, sheet, reuse in video).

```bash
npx skills add vargHQ/skills --skill varg-character-absurd                # Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Gemini CLI, OpenCode…
gh skill install vargHQ/skills varg-character-absurd --agent github-copilot --scope user
# or all 82 skills as a Claude Code plugin:
claude plugin marketplace add vargHQ/skills
claude plugin install varg@varg
```

| | |
|---|---|
| Makes | Original mascot turnaround sheet |
| Needs | a varg account (OAuth through the varg MCP) or `VARG_API_KEY` |
| Typical cost | ~$0.06 per sheet (Nano Banana 2.1, tested) |
| Uses | varg API, Nano Banana 2.1 |
| Works in | Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot, OpenCode and other Agent Skills tools |
| Agent instructions | [SKILL.md](./SKILL.md) (v1.0.0) |

## Ask your agent

- "Make an original brainrot-style character: a croissant that is also a pigeon, wearing tiny white sneakers"
- "Design a grumpy cactus mascot for my plant shop as a 3D family-film turnaround sheet"
- "Create three absurd food creatures for a micro-drama series in a clay stop-motion look"
